title: Inventory numbers people could act on.
shortTitle: A shared truth across disconnected inventory.
description: Manufacturers needed their existing inventory systems to agree. I founded Closphere around a canonical data model, continuous reconciliation, and visibility into failures that would otherwise stay silent.
trust: Trust mechanism: continuous reconciliation against the source ERP, plus silent-failure detection.
scope: I owned discovery, product, the inventory model, growth, and the technology sale and led a 12-person team.
heroCaption: A matching balance and a healthy sync are different signals. The interface makes both visible.
supportingCaption: Systems map into a shared inventory model, so downstream views do not need a separate interpretation for every source.

decision.chose: A canonical inventory model with configuration-driven mappings.
decision.over: Build a bespoke integration for each customer.
decision.evidence: Discovery with 50+ customers revealed common inventory entities across systems.
decision.tradeoff: Invest in the shared model before optimizing individual connectors.
decision.cost: Upfront modeling work and tighter boundaries around custom requests.

systemDetails: Item master, units of measure, multi-location stock, batch/lot, transaction types.

Continuous checks against the source ERP.
Surface mismatches and detect silent sync failures.

sections.label: The Problem
sections.title: The same stock had conflicting stories.
paragraphs: Manufacturers worked across ERPs, spreadsheets, and operational records. Units of measure, locations, and transactions did not line up. When the numbers disagreed, people had to reconcile them manually before making a decision.

sections.label: What I Found
sections.title: Customers needed agreement, not another replacement.
paragraphs: Discovery with 50+ customers surfaced shared concepts: items, units, locations, batches, and transactions. The systems differed in how they represented those concepts. The opportunity was a common model that could sit across them.

sections.label: What Shipped
sections.title: Reconciliation as a product capability.
paragraphs: Closphere mapped source systems into a canonical inventory model, then used that model for dashboards and alerts. Continuous reconciliation compared the result against the source ERP.
Silent-failure detection made stopped sync visible. A dashboard could look complete while its data had stopped changing, so connection health needed to be part of the product experience.

sections.label: Outcomes
sections.title: A foundation that customers could keep using.
paragraphs: Closphere reached 63 paying customers, 1K+ users, and 112 locations. Inventory record accuracy improved from 75% to 95%, stockouts fell 32%, and reconciliation effort fell 70%+.
Onboarding went from 6+ weeks to under 7 days. Referrals drove approximately 30% of new business. The business exited through a technology/IP sale.

sections.label: What I Learned
sections.title: The data model was the product.
paragraphs: Connectors and dashboards only became useful when the underlying meaning was consistent. As a founder, I also learned to treat team capacity as a product constraint before committing to customization.
